description: BaSeL semi-empirical theoretical SED libraries: theoretical spectra (Kurucz ATLAS9 and others) recalibrated onto empirical color-temperature relations, published by the author (Pieter Westera, UFABC) as one tarball per version plus a format ReadMe. BaSeL 2.2 (Lejeune, Cuisinier & Buser 1998) calibrates at solar metallicity; BaSeL 3.1 (Westera et al. 2002) recalibrates per metallicity and ships TWO calibration variants (WLBC99, PADOVA2000) in the one tarball — genuinely different recalibrations at the same node sets, a read-side grid selection. The complete inventory below is byte-verified (2026-11-18); the blueprint declares all three files.

BaSeL2_2.tar.gz.content: BaSeL 2.2: 19 lbc96_<metallicity>.cor files, [M/H] -5.0 to +1.0 (m50 m45 m40 m35 m30 m25 m20 m15 m10 m05 m03 m02 m01 p00 p01 p02 p03 p05 p10)

BaSeL3_1.tar.gz.content: BaSeL 3.1: WLBC99/ and PADOVA2000/ directories, each 6 wlbc99_<metallicity>.cor files ([M/H] -2.0 -1.5 -1.0 -0.5 0.0 +0.5) + 12 calibration_<metallicity>.{dw,gi} empirical color tables per variant (dw = dwarf, gi = giant)

BaSeL_ReadMe.txt.content: the author's format description (Kurucz format; flags the flux per-steradian ambiguity)

format_facts: one ASCII file per metallicity; all spectra of the file share one wavelength grid stated once at the top: 1221 points in nm (FORTRAN 8f10.1), 9.1 nm to 160000 nm, IDENTICAL across every file of both versions

one 176-line block per spectrum: parameter line (2i6, 4f6.2) = spectrum number, Teff, log g, [Fe/H], plus two columns the author marks unused (published values are 0.0 or 2.0 and 0.0 or 1.25); then 175 lines of 1221 flux values (7e11.4)

stated flux unit erg/s/cm/cm/Hz; bolometric closure of the published numbers (integral over frequency = sigma T^4 / 4 pi to 0.1-0.5% for Teff 5000-50000 K, 0.5% residue at 2000 K, both versions and both variants) pins it as the Eddington flux per steradian — surface flux = 4 pi H. The papers pin the bolometric integral to the effective-temperature definition and the author's ReadMe flags the 4pi ambiguity; neither states the steradian convention — the files themselves are the decisive evidence

the per-metallicity (Teff, log g) node sets DIFFER (3.1: 450-459 blocks per file; 2.2: 375-467), so the 3-axis (Teff, log g, [M/H]) grid has large honest holes; BaSeL 2.2 additionally holds 29 blocks whose [Fe/H] column disagrees with the filename's metallicity (p01: 20 blocks stating 0.2; p02: 3 stating 1.0; p03: 6 stating 1.0)

coverage.3.1: Teff 2000-50000 K (68 steps), log g -1.02 to 5.5 (19 values, following dwarf/giant sequences), [M/H] in {-2.0, -1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0.0, +0.5}
coverage.2.2: Teff 2000-50000 K, log g -1.02 to 5.5, [M/H] in 19 steps from -5.0 to +1.0
